one_line: Agents safely inspect a page and assemble missing WebMCP tools on demand.
what_it_does: Provides meta-tools to inspect page scope, propose/register a typed tool, or execute one-off code, demonstrated on a happiness dashboard.
leverage_rationale: The product directly addresses the empty-tool-surface problem by making the agent a controlled author of page-specific WebMCP capabilities; ordinary UI driving cannot match the structured, reusable surface as reliably.
leverage_evidence: Three meta-tools are described: inspect scope, suggest/register tool, and execute code mode.
The demo adds a missing 7.4 filter through the app's own function and re-renders the table/chart.
Frame sheets show dashboard state changes and a confirmation/modal step.
execution_rationale: The packet gives a coherent end-to-end claim and frames show a consistent dashboard workflow, but no transcript and limited legibility cap confidence.
execution_evidence: Frames show a world-happiness dashboard, intermediate modal, and filtered chart/table states.
The written scenario specifies twelve rows becoming four after the approved filter.
impact_rationale: If safe dynamic tool creation works as claimed, it could materially expand agent capability across the otherwise tool-less web, with clear value for agents and site builders.
impact_evidence: Targets the stated adoption gap between WebMCP standards and sites exposing useful tools.
Demonstrates a concrete missing-filter use case.
creativity_rationale: Treating registerTool and toolchange as an agent-authored, safety-gated surface is a novel and ambitious interpretation of WebMCP.
creativity_evidence: Agent-generated lasting tools plus one-off code mode form an unusual meta-tool design.
The concept explicitly distinguishes inspect, propose, approve, and execute.
usability_note: The confirmation boundary is promising, though dynamic tool creation and code mode add complexity.
red_flags: No video transcript; frame text is not fully legible.
Safety of generated code is asserted more than independently demonstrated.
advance_reason: High leverage and originality with enough coherent product evidence to merit advancement.

one_line: A live WebMCP manifest removes capabilities when evidence becomes stale and stops at human authority gates.
what_it_does: Runs an identity-recovery mission whose available tools are compiled from current evidence, handling expiry, retry, handoff, and a structured receipt.
leverage_rationale: Changing the callable tool surface itself in response to evidence and authority is the product; a general browser agent cannot comparably guarantee stale capabilities are removed.
leverage_evidence: Claims nine static/four compiled tools with five stale capabilities removed.
Frames explicitly show toolset reduction, expired challenge, recorded state, and human-only last door.
Confirmation is deliberately not registered as a WebMCP tool.
execution_rationale: The staged flow is coherent and the frame sequence visibly covers challenge, expiration/rejection, state recording, and human handoff; exact end-to-end details remain partly unreadable.
execution_evidence: Frames show the controlled-link/state-challenge/human-presence stages.
Frames show the agent stopping rather than claiming human confirmation.
Written packet describes fresh-event retry and structured completion receipt.
impact_rationale: Safe capability revocation and explicit human authority address a serious reliability and governance problem in stateful browser agents.
impact_evidence: Targets stale authentication, checkout approval, and production-change risks.
Fail-closed handoff is demonstrated as the central outcome.
creativity_rationale: The concept makes an evidence-compiled manifest, rather than a static tool list, the core interaction model and pursues it deeply.
creativity_evidence: Evidence changes cause tools to appear/disappear.
The 'last door' metaphor is implemented as an authority boundary, not just messaging.
usability_note: The staged authority model is understandable, though manifest changes may require careful explanation.
red_flags: Some frame annotations are promotional and small.
No transcript limits verification of exact calls.
standouts: WebMCP is central rather than decorative.
advance_reason: Exceptional leverage with a coherent, safety-relevant demonstration.

one_line: Students search and inspect 1,331 college lacrosse programs through a synchronized agent and map.
what_it_does: Exposes narrow read-only search and program-detail tools that synchronize filters, counts, markers, and visible school details.
leverage_rationale: Typed search and stable IDs improve precision and shared state, but a capable general agent could achieve much of the same map search with meaningful UI friction.
leverage_evidence: Two narrow read-only tools are described.
Frames show map markers and filtering/results states.
The same filters and map are claimed to update from agent search.
execution_rationale: The map-first product appears coherent and the frames show repeated map/filter/detail states, but agent execution is not directly visible.
execution_evidence: Frames show a populated North American program map and filter panel.
Written workflow specifies search followed by visible synchronized details.
impact_rationale: Student-athletes and families have a concrete discovery problem across fragmented collegiate pathways; a unified searchable map is credible value.
impact_evidence: Claims coverage across NCAA, NAIA, NJCAA, MCLA, and WCLA.
Use case connects discovery with academics, admissions, athletics, and fit.
creativity_rationale: A map-first college sports directory with agent search is a competent, useful synthesis but not an especially novel interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Agent-to-map synchronization is a fresh integration angle.
Core directory/map concept is familiar.
usability_note: Natural-language discovery plus a visible map appears approachable and keeps the student in control.
red_flags: Contact sheets do not show an agent transcript or tool trace.
Data quality and freshness are not independently evidenced.
standouts: Narrow tool design avoids overclaiming agent authority.
advance_reason: Strong audience fit and solid product execution, though leverage and novelty are moderate.

one_line: A privacy-first support navigator lets agents orchestrate typed, auditable help while humans control sensitive facts.
what_it_does: Offers structured discovery, case analysis, explanation, comparison, demo-case loading, and checklist tools backed by a shared deterministic rules engine.
leverage_rationale: Typed domain tools and shared deterministic state substantially reduce scraping and ambiguity in rule-heavy support navigation; the agent-human division is central.
leverage_evidence: Six structured tools and a shared JavaScript rule engine are described.
The written design keeps matched/missing conditions visible and logs meaningful actions.
Frames show a structured support/workflow interface, though not a readable trace.
execution_rationale: The architecture is coherent, but the packet has no gallery images and the frame evidence is low-resolution, so end-to-end completeness is only plausibly shown.
execution_evidence: Written workflow covers discovery through next-step checklist.
Frames show a consistent product interface and staged content.
impact_rationale: Navigating public benefits and support programs is a high-value problem for people facing complex eligibility rules, and auditable assistance could meaningfully reduce friction.
impact_evidence: Explicitly targets rule-heavy public-service support navigation.
Human control of sensitive facts and deterministic explanations fit the audience's trust needs.
creativity_rationale: The human-controls-facts/agent-orchestrates model is a thoughtful synthesis with meaningful privacy and auditability ambition.
creativity_evidence: Shared rule engine serves both UI and WebMCP.
Agent actions are designed to remain inspectable rather than deciding eligibility.
usability_note: Auditable matched/missing conditions could make a complex domain understandable, though the workflow may be dense.
red_flags: No Devpost gallery images and limited legible visual proof.
Eligibility rules are described as illustrative/demo data.
standouts: Deterministic shared engine and audit log.
advance_reason: High potential impact and meaningful WebMCP leverage outweigh thin execution evidence.

one_line: An agent finds weak listings, separates verified from conflicting facts, and drafts safer improvements for merchant approval.
what_it_does: Searches a synthetic catalog, inspects product truth, prepares verified-only listing copy, and blocks approval/publishing until a merchant acts.
leverage_rationale: Structured product-truth tools materially improve factual reliability and shared approval state over UI scraping, although a general agent could eventually reproduce parts of the flow.
leverage_evidence: Four WebMCP tools cover search, truth inspection, preparation, and approval boundary.
Written design distinguishes verified, conflicting, and missing facts.
Frames show agent-ready tools, product score, facts panels, and waiting-for-agent/human action states.
execution_rationale: The dashboard and staged workflow appear coherent, with a concrete synthetic catalog, selected product, score, fact categories, and human checkpoint.
execution_evidence: Frames show 500 synthetic products, selected item, health score, verification cards, and listing preparation control.
Publishing is explicitly blocked before approval.
impact_rationale: Merchants have a real problem with incomplete or contradictory supplier facts; safer listing preparation can prevent misleading commerce content.
impact_evidence: Problem-solution fit is explicit and concrete.
Human approval is preserved for consequential publishing.
creativity_rationale: Verified-fact gating for agent-generated commerce copy is a strong, thoughtful angle on a familiar listing workflow.
creativity_evidence: Product Truth separates conflicting and missing data before drafting.
Agent speed is paired with a hard approval boundary.
usability_note: The staged dashboard and explicit readiness/waiting states support merchant review.
red_flags: Catalog is synthetic, so production data integration is unproven.
Frames show readiness more clearly than a completed tool invocation.
advance_reason: Well-scoped commerce workflow with credible execution and safety-aware leverage.

one_line: A scored city guide lets people and agents search venues, check hours, draft itineraries, and return booking links together.
what_it_does: Exposes read-oriented venue search, detail, hours, itinerary, and booking-link capabilities over a large multi-city catalog.
leverage_rationale: Structured live venue data avoids scraping and makes planning more reliable, but a general agent can perform similar discovery with UI browsing at some friction.
leverage_evidence: Five WebMCP tools are described over search, venue, hours, itinerary, and booking data.
Frames show a polished city-guide page and curated venue content, but not tool calls.
Written design keeps tools read-only and booking as a human action.
execution_rationale: The product description is coherent, but the packet has no gallery images and the contact sheet mostly shows static editorial UI without visible agent completion.
execution_evidence: Frames show loaded guide, featured content, and venue/editorial layout.
Written packet specifies a live venue API and one-page planning flow.
impact_rationale: Planning a night out is a recognizable desire with clear convenience value, and local venue data benefits from current hours and booking links.
impact_evidence: Specific scenario: dinner then cocktails within walking distance.
Claims coverage of 19,000 venues across 24 cities.
creativity_rationale: Agent-native co-planning on a scored city guide is a useful synthesis, but the underlying guide and itinerary pattern is familiar.
creativity_evidence: Shared human/agent surface and scored-not-starred framing.
Read-only planning plus human save is a sensible interaction choice.
usability_note: A single page and conversational planning model are easy to understand, though live-data caveats matter.
red_flags: No gallery images; visuals are mostly static marketing/editorial screens.
Live API and booking behavior are asserted, not visibly verified.
standouts: Good human judgment versus agent legwork division.
advance_reason: Promising but thin execution/tool evidence and only moderate WebMCP delta.

one_line: A construction field-review workspace lets ChatGPT read live drawing context and draft coordinate-pinned findings while people verify and issue.
what_it_does: Provides six project-bound tools for context, findings, review lifecycle, draft creation/update, and briefing preparation, with verification and issuance reserved for humans.
leverage_rationale: Binding structured writes to the open project, discipline, numbered review, and drawing coordinates gives an agent precise shared state that UI automation would handle unreliably.
leverage_evidence: Six tools are registered on every project screen, including context, open findings, review lifecycle, draft finding, update/verify, and briefing.
Written example pins a draft at 62% across and 49% down on sheet A2.02.
Frames show review lists and the registered-tool panel.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a substantial, internally consistent field-review workspace and the frames show its review/finding surfaces and tool registry, though final issuance is intentionally not automated.
execution_evidence: Frames show PunchPilot review dashboard and six named site tools.
Written flow covers project, disciplines, drawings, findings, photos, status history, checklists, and briefing.
impact_rationale: Construction reviewers have a concrete need to convert on-site observations into traceable drawing-linked records; reducing repetitive data entry while preserving verification is credible value.
impact_evidence: Specific field-review workflow and drawing-coordinate use case.
Human retains verification and issuance, appropriate to consequential records.
creativity_rationale: The drawing-bound, project-identity-aware agent collaboration is a notably original application of WebMCP beyond generic summarization.
creativity_evidence: Draft pins are page-aware percentages on a filed drawing set.
Tool design explicitly prevents the agent from verifying/completing/issuing.
usability_note: A reviewer-centered workspace with concise draft actions is promising, though construction records are inherently dense.
red_flags: The frame contact sheets do not visibly show a completed briefing or issued report.
Exact write/verification behavior is primarily packet-described.
standouts: Strong domain binding and safety boundary.
advance_reason: High leverage, strong domain fit, and distinctive shared-state interaction.

one_line: An AI teammate turns emergency radio information into confirmable map updates while keeping dispatchers in control.
what_it_does: Proposes hazard-zone/map changes from chaotic 911 radio calls and routes them through human approval.
leverage_rationale: Structured map proposals and confirmation could reduce fragile GIS clicking in a high-pressure workflow, but the packet provides no video evidence to verify the WebMCP-specific delta.
leverage_evidence: Written pitch centers on precise, confirmable map updates.
Submission packaging visibly emphasizes hazard zone, AI draft proposals, and human approval.
No frame sheets were submitted, so invocation and shared-state claims cannot be checked.
execution_rationale: The concept and packaging are coherent, but there is no submitted video/frame evidence and the written packet is truncated, so execution is thinly evidenced.
execution_evidence: Devpost packaging screenshot shows a three-stage concept: hazard zone, AI draft proposals, human approval.
No product-motion evidence is included.
impact_rationale: Emergency dispatchers and responders have an urgent, specific problem where faster, confirmable map updates could materially improve safety and coordination.
impact_evidence: Targets life-critical wildfire/flood and emergency-radio workflows.
Human approval is explicitly retained for consequential map updates.
creativity_rationale: Applying agent-native structured proposals to emergency GIS updates is ambitious and memorable, even though depth is not verifiable here.
creativity_evidence: Combines radio interpretation, map editing, and confirmation in one agent teammate concept.
Explicit hazard-zone proposal workflow.
usability_note: The approval-oriented concept could fit dispatchers, but usability under emergency pressure is unproven.
red_flags: No video frame sheets submitted.
High-stakes claims lack observed runtime evidence.
Public repository is absent.
standouts: Human approval is central rather than an afterthought.
advance_reason: Impact and ambition are high, but missing product-motion evidence makes execution and eligibility too uncertain.

one_line: Agents negotiate meeting times in a shared session while humans vote, counter-propose, and approve the final slot.
what_it_does: Registers seven tools for reading event state, joining, voting with reasons, counter-proposing, ranking slots, and reporting winners, with a human organizer lock.
leverage_rationale: Multiple agents and humans participating in the same live negotiation log is a materially different shared-state interaction than an agent clicking a poll UI.
leverage_evidence: Seven tools support read/join/vote/counter-propose/rank actions.
Frames show candidate times, participants, negotiation log, and counter-proposals.
Every action is tagged HUMAN or AGENT and final lock is human-only.
execution_rationale: The frame sequence shows populated creation and review/negotiation states with a coherent progression, though technical invocation details are not visible.
execution_evidence: Frames show create-event form, candidate-time review, participants, negotiation log, and counter-proposals.
Written packet describes a four-tool first-try chain from state read to winner report.
impact_rationale: Scheduling across conflicting constraints is common and tedious; mixed human/agent negotiation can save effort while preserving organizer authority.
impact_evidence: Specific group-scheduling problem and candidate-time workflow.
Shared log makes agent actions visible to participants.
creativity_rationale: Treating each person's agent as an equal negotiation participant, with votes and counter-proposals in shared state, is a memorable interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Agent-mediated negotiation rather than a single assistant choosing a slot.
Human and agent actions coexist in one auditable log.
usability_note: The familiar event form plus visible negotiation log should make the novel agent role legible.
red_flags: No direct tool-call transcript in frames.
Actual multi-party real-time behavior is packet-claimed.
advance_reason: Distinctive, high-leverage collaboration model with strong visible workflow evidence.

one_line: A Chrome extension derives proposed WebMCP tools from existing forms, labels, and ARIA metadata.
what_it_does: Reads DOM accessibility metadata, generates tool names/schemas/risk/confidence with provenance, then lets users approve registrations.
leverage_rationale: Automating the conversion of existing accessible UI semantics into reviewed WebMCP capabilities addresses a major adoption bottleneck; it is more than a browser agent clicking controls.
leverage_evidence: Written design maps forms, buttons, labels, and ARIA attributes to typed schemas.
Generated candidates include risk classification, confidence, and exact evidence attributes.
Frames show ChatGPT-like workflow and map/UI states, but not a clearly legible extension approval screen.
execution_rationale: The concept is technically coherent, but the packet's frame evidence is difficult to attribute to the extension's core proposal/approval flow and no direct invocation trace is visible.
execution_evidence: Written packet includes a concrete registerTool object and execution path.
Frames show a browser/assistant workflow but limited readable extension-specific states.
impact_rationale: If robust, it could lower the cost of making the existing web agent-compatible and leverage accessibility work already present across many sites.
impact_evidence: Targets the hand-authoring and maintenance barrier for WebMCP adoption.
Uses existing accessibility metadata as a broad source of capability contracts.
creativity_rationale: Reframing accessibility metadata as latent agent capability contracts is an original and ambitious idea.
creativity_evidence: Evidence-backed generation rather than opaque scraping.
Human approval and risk classification are part of the interaction model.
usability_note: Approval with provenance is promising, but generated tools may require substantial review and error handling.
red_flags: Core extension UI is not clearly visible in the supplied frame reading.
Generated handlers may be fragile for ambiguous or dynamic controls.
standouts: Provenance and risk review make automation more trustworthy.
advance_reason: High adoption potential and originality, with execution evidence weaker than the concept.
